full_text: (a) A person commits the offense of aggravated assault when he or she assaults: (1) With intent to murder, to rape, or to rob; (2) With a deadly weapon or with any object, device, or instrument which, when used offensively against a person, is likely to or actually does result in serious bodily injury; or (3) A person or persons without legal justification by discharging a firearm from within a motor vehicle toward a person or persons. (b) Except as provided in subsections (c) and (d) of this Code section, aggravated assault is a felony punishable by imprisonment for not less than one nor more than 20 years. (c) Upon a first conviction for aggravated assault under subsection (a) of this Code section, the defendant shall be punished by imprisonment for not less than five nor more than 20 years. (d) Upon a second or subsequent conviction for aggravated assault under subsection (a) of this Code section, the defendant shall be punished by imprisonment for not less than ten nor more than 20 years.

(a) A person commits the offense of simple assault when he or she either: (1) Attempts to commit a violent injury to the person of another; or (2) Commits an act which places another in reasonable apprehension of immediately receiving a violent injury. (b) Except as provided in subsections (c) and (d) of this Code section, a person convicted of the offense of simple assault shall be punished as for a misdemeanor. (c) A person convicted of the offense of simple assault against a person who is 65 years of age or older shall be punished by imprisonment for not less than 30 days nor more than 12 months and by a fine of not more than $1,000.00. (d) A person convicted of the offense of simple assault by strangulation shall be punished by imprisonment for not less than one year nor more than five years.

(a) A person commits the offense of battery when he or she intentionally causes substantial physical harm or visible bodily harm to another. (b) A person commits the offense of battery when, in a public place and with criminal intent, he or she intentionally strikes another person or touches another person in a rude and insolent manner. (c) Except as provided in subsections (d) and (e) of this Code section, a person who commits the offense of battery shall be guilty of a misdemeanor. (d) A person who commits the offense of battery against a person who is 65 years of age or older shall be guilty of a felony and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punished by imprisonment for not less than one nor more than five years and by a fine of not more than $5,000.00. (e) A person who commits the offense of battery by strangulation shall be guilty of a felony and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punished by imprisonment for not less than one nor more than five years.

(a) A person commits the offense of criminal attempt when, with intent to commit a specific crime, he or she performs any act which constitutes a substantial step toward the commission of that crime. (b) It is no defense to a prosecution for criminal attempt that the crime charged to have been attempted was, under the attendant circumstances, factually or legally impossible of commission, if such crime could have been committed had the attendant circumstances been as the person believed them to be. (c) A person convicted of criminal attempt shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than one-half of the maximum imprisonment prescribed for the offense attempted, or by a fine not to exceed one-half of the maximum fine prescribed for the offense attempted, or both.

(a) A person commits the offense of theft by taking when he or she unlawfully takes or, being in lawful possession thereof, unlawfully appropriates any property of another with the intention of depriving him or her of the property, regardless of the manner in which the property is taken or appropriated. (b) Except as provided in subsection (c) of this Code section, any person who commits theft by taking property which exceeds $500.00 in value shall be guilty of a felony and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punished by imprisonment for not less than one nor more than ten years. (c) Any person who commits theft by taking property which does not exceed $500.00 in value shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.

(a) A person commits the offense of theft by deception when he or she obtains property by any deceitful means or artful practice with the intention of depriving the owner of the property. (b) Except as provided in subsection (c) of this Code section, any person who commits theft by deception which involves property exceeding $500.00 in value shall be guilty of a felony and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punished by imprisonment for not less than one nor more than ten years. (c) Any person who commits theft by deception which involves property not exceeding $500.00 in value shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.

(a) A person commits the offense of theft by conversion when he or she lawfully obtains possession of property belonging to another with the intention of depriving him or her of the property and converts the property to his or her own use. (b) Except as provided in subsection (c) of this Code section, any person who commits theft by conversion which involves property exceeding $500.00 in value shall be guilty of a felony and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punished by imprisonment for not less than one nor more than ten years. (c) Any person who commits theft by conversion which involves property not exceeding $500.00 in value shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.

(a) A person commits the offense of theft of services when he or she obtains services which he or she knows are available only for compensation by deception, threat, coercion, or by stealth or by any other means to avoid payment for the services. (b) Except as provided in subsection (c) of this Code section, any person who commits theft of services which involves services valued at more than $500.00 shall be guilty of a felony and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punished by imprisonment for not less than one nor more than ten years. (c) Any person who commits theft of services which involves services valued at $500.00 or less shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.

(a) A person commits the offense of robbery when, with intent to commit theft, he or she takes property of another from the person or the immediate presence of another: (1) By use of force; (2) By intimidation, by the use of threat or coercion, or by placing such person in reasonable fear of immediately receiving bodily injury; or (3) By sudden snatching. (b) A person convicted of the offense of robbery shall be punished by imprisonment for not less than one year nor more than 20 years.

(a) A person commits the offense of armed robbery when, with intent to commit theft, he or she takes property of another from the person or the immediate presence of another by use of an offensive weapon, or any replica, article, or device having the appearance of such weapon. (b) A person convicted of armed robbery shall be punished by imprisonment for not less than one year nor more than 20 years.

(a) A contract is an agreement between two or more parties for the doing or not doing of some specified thing. (b) To constitute a valid contract, there must be parties able to contract, a consideration moving to the contract, the assent of the parties to the terms of the contract, and a subject matter upon which the contract can operate. (c) The term 'contract' includes all agreements, whether written or oral, for the sale of goods, the rendering of services, or the lease of property.

(a) To constitute consideration, a performance or a return promise must be bargained for. (b) A performance or return promise is bargained for if it is sought by the promisor in exchange for his promise and is given by the promisee in exchange for that promise. (c) The performance may consist of: (1) An act other than a promise; or (2) A forbearance; or (3) The creation, modification, or destruction of a legal relation. (d) The performance or return promise may be given to the promisor or to some other person. It may be given by the promisee or by some other person.

(a) All persons are capable of contracting except minors, persons of unsound mind, and persons deprived of civil rights. (b) A minor is a person who has not reached the age of 18 years. (c) A person of unsound mind is one who does not have sufficient mental capacity to understand the nature and consequences of his or her acts. (d) A person deprived of civil rights is one who has been convicted of a felony and has not had his or her civil rights restored.

(a) Fraud in the inducement of a contract occurs when a party makes a false representation of a material fact, with intent to deceive, and the other party relies on that representation to his or her detriment. (b) Fraud in the execution of a contract occurs when a party is deceived as to the nature of the document he or she is signing. (c) Remedies for fraud include rescission of the contract and damages.

(a) Duress in the formation of a contract occurs when a party is compelled to enter into a contract by threat of unlawful action. (b) Economic duress occurs when a party is compelled to enter into a contract by threat of financial harm. (c) A contract entered into under duress is voidable by the party subjected to duress.

(a) A person shall not drive or be in actual physical control of any moving vehicle while: (1) Under the influence of alcohol to the extent that it is less safe for the person to drive; (2) Under the influence of any drug to the extent that it is less safe for the person to drive; or (3) Under the combined influence of alcohol and a drug to the extent that it is less safe for the person to drive. (b) Upon a first conviction, a person convicted of violating subsection (a) of this Code section shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and shall be punished by: (1) A fine of not less than $300.00 nor more than $1,000.00; and (2) Imprisonment for not less than 10 days nor more than 12 months. (c) Upon a second conviction, a person convicted of violating subsection (a) of this Code section shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and shall be punished by: (1) A fine of not less than $600.00 nor more than $1,000.00; and (2) Imprisonment for not less than 30 days nor more than 12 months. (d) Upon a third or subsequent conviction, a person convicted of violating subsection (a) of this Code section shall be guilty of a felony and shall be punished by: (1) A fine of not less than $1,000.00 nor more than $5,000.00; and (2) Imprisonment for not less than 120 days nor more than five years.

(a) Any person who drives any vehicle with willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property is guilty of reckless driving. Violation of the provisions of this Code section is a misdemeanor punishable by imprisonment for not less than 30 days nor more than 12 months and by a fine of not more than $1,000.00. (b) Upon a second conviction within a five-year period of time, the defendant shall be guilty of a misdemeanor of a high and aggravated nature and shall be punished by imprisonment for not less than 60 days nor more than 12 months and by a fine of not more than $2,500.00. (c) Upon a third or subsequent conviction within a five-year period of time, the defendant shall be guilty of a felony and shall be punished by imprisonment for not less than one year nor more than five years and by a fine of not more than $5,000.00.

section_name: Hit and run; duty of driver to stop at or return to scene of accident
full_text: (a) The driver of any vehicle involved in an accident resulting in injury to or death of any person or damage to any vehicle or other property shall immediately stop such vehicle at the scene of the accident or as close thereto as possible and shall forthwith return to and in every event shall remain at the scene of the accident until he or she has fulfilled the requirements of Code Section 40-6-273. (b) Any person who violates the provisions of subsection (a) of this Code section shall be guilty of a misdemeanor of a high and aggravated nature and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punished by imprisonment for not less than 120 days nor more than 12 months and by a fine of not more than $1,000.00. (c) If the accident results in injury to or death of any person, any person who violates the provisions of subsection (a) of this Code section shall be guilty of a felony and, upon conviction thereof, shall be punished by imprisonment for not less than one year nor more than five years and by a fine of not more than $5,000.00.

(a) When a person is killed by the negligence of another, damages which are recoverable for the benefit of the decedent's surviving spouse, children, or other dependents may include: (1) The value of the life of the decedent to the decedent; (2) The value of the decedent's services to the decedent's spouse, children, or other dependents; and (3) The full value of the pecuniary loss to the decedent's surviving spouse, children, or other dependents. (b) The amount of damages awarded shall not be diminished by the contributory negligence of the decedent. (c) The right of action for wrongful death shall survive the decedent and may be brought by the decedent's personal representative.

(a) Every employer shall secure the payment of compensation to his or her employees and their dependents for injury or death by accident arising out of and in the course of the employment. (b) The State Board of Workers' Compensation shall administer the workers' compensation law and shall have jurisdiction to hear and determine all questions of law and fact arising under this chapter. (c) The maximum compensation payable for total disability shall be 66 2/3 percent of the employee's average weekly wage, not to exceed the maximum weekly benefit established by the board.

(a) In all cases where the custody of any child or children is at issue between the parents, there shall be no prima facie right to the custody of the child in either parent. The court shall look to and determine solely from the evidence what is for the best interest of the child or children. (b) In determining the best interests of the child, the court shall consider: (1) The love, affection, bonding, and emotional ties existing between each parent and the child; (2) The love, affection, bonding, and emotional ties existing between the child and his or her siblings, half siblings, and stepsiblings and the residence of such other children; (3) The capacity and disposition of each parent to give the child love, affection, and guidance and to continue the education and rearing of the child; (4) The capacity and disposition of each parent to provide the child with food, clothing, medical care, and other material needs; (5) The length of time the child has lived in a stable, satisfactory environment and the desirability of maintaining continuity; (6) The permanence, as a family unit, of the existing or proposed custodial home or homes; (7) The moral fitness of each parent; (8) The mental and physical health of each parent; (9) The home, school, and community record and history of the child, as well as any health or educational special needs of the child; (10) The willingness and ability of each parent to facilitate and encourage a close and continuing parent-child relationship between the child and the other parent; (11) Any recommendation by a court appointed custody evaluator or guardian ad litem; (12) Any evidence of family violence or sexual, mental, or physical child abuse or criminal history of either parent; and (13) Any other relevant factor.

(a) In all legal proceedings for child support, the court shall base its award on the needs of the child and the ability of each parent to pay. (b) The court shall consider the following factors in determining the amount of child support: (1) The standard of living and situation of the parties; (2) The duration of the marriage; (3) The conduct of each party with respect to the marriage; (4) The financial resources and needs of each party; (5) The financial resources and needs of the child or children; (6) The earning capacity of each party; (7) The age and physical and emotional condition of each party; (8) The educational background of each party; (9) The contribution of each party to the marriage, including homemaking and child care contributions; (10) The time necessary for either party to acquire sufficient education or training to enable that party to find appropriate employment; (11) The tax treatment and consequences to each party; (12) The alimony or separate maintenance awarded or received; and (13) Any other relevant factor. (c) The court may deviate from the child support guidelines if it finds that the application of the guidelines would be unjust or inappropriate.

(a) Alimony may be granted in cases of divorce, separate maintenance, or annulment. (b) In determining whether to award alimony and the amount of alimony to be awarded, the court shall consider: (1) The standard of living during the marriage; (2) The duration of the marriage; (3) The age and physical and emotional condition of each party; (4) The financial resources of each party; (5) The contribution of each party to the marriage, including services rendered in homemaking, child care, education, and career building of the other party; (6) The time necessary for either party to acquire sufficient education or training to enable that party to find appropriate employment; (7) The earning capacity of each party; and (8) Any other relevant factor. (c) Alimony may be awarded in lump sum, periodic payments, or both.

(a) One or more persons may incorporate a business corporation by filing with the Secretary of State articles of incorporation which shall be executed and acknowledged by each incorporator. (b) The articles of incorporation shall set forth: (1) The name of the corporation; (2) The number of shares the corporation is authorized to issue; (3) The street address of the corporation's initial registered office and the name of its initial registered agent at that office; (4) The name and address of each incorporator; and (5) The period of duration of the corporation if other than perpetual. (c) The articles of incorporation may set forth any or all of the corporation's bylaws.

(a) Each corporation shall have power to: (1) Have perpetual succession by its corporate name unless a limited period of duration is stated in its articles of incorporation; (2) Sue and be sued, complain and defend, in its corporate name; (3) Have a corporate seal which may be altered at will and use the same by causing it or a facsimile thereof to be impressed or affixed or in any other manner reproduced; (4) Purchase, take, receive, lease, take by gift, devise, or bequest, or otherwise acquire, own, hold, improve, use, and otherwise deal in and with real or personal property, or any interest therein, wherever situated; (5) Sell, convey, mortgage, pledge, lease, exchange, transfer, and otherwise dispose of all or any part of its property and assets; (6) Lend money to and otherwise assist its employees, officers, and directors; (7) Purchase and maintain insurance on behalf of any person who is or was a director, officer, employee, or agent of the corporation; (8) Make donations for the public welfare or for charitable, scientific, or educational purposes; and (9) Transact any lawful business.

(a) A lease is a contract by which one party, called the lessor, gives to another party, called the lessee, the right to possess and use property for a specified time and for a specified consideration called rent. (b) A lease may be written or oral. (c) A lease for more than one year must be in writing to be enforceable. (d) A lease may include covenants, conditions, and agreements as the parties may desire.

section_name: Rights and duties of lessor and lessee
full_text: (a) The lessor covenants that the lessee shall peaceably and quietly enjoy the leased premises. (b) The lessee covenants to pay the rent at the time and in the manner provided in the lease. (c) The lessee shall not use the premises for any unlawful purpose. (d) The lessee shall comply with all applicable laws, ordinances, and regulations. (e) The lessee shall keep the premises in good repair and condition. (f) Upon termination of the lease, the lessee shall surrender possession of the premises to the lessor.

(a) A landlord may evict a tenant for: (1) Nonpayment of rent; (2) Violation of the lease terms; (3) Use of the premises for unlawful purposes; or (4) Other good cause. (b) Before evicting a tenant, the landlord must give written notice to the tenant. (c) The notice period shall be: (1) Seven days for nonpayment of rent; (2) 30 days for other violations. (d) If the tenant does not comply with the notice, the landlord may file a dispossessory action in court. (e) The court may issue a writ of possession if the landlord proves entitlement to eviction.

(a) A partnership is an association of two or more persons to carry on as co-owners a business for profit. (b) Persons who share profits and losses are presumed to be partners. (c) A partnership may be general or limited. (d) A partnership is not a separate legal entity from its partners.

(a) Employment in Georgia is at-will unless otherwise specified in a contract. (b) An employer may terminate an employee at any time for any lawful reason or for no reason. (c) An employee may quit employment at any time for any lawful reason or for no reason. (d) Exceptions to at-will employment include contracts, statutes, and public policy.

(a) An employer may not terminate an employee for: (1) Refusing to violate the law; (2) Exercising a legal right; or (3) Performing a public duty. (b) An employee terminated in violation of public policy may bring a tort action for wrongful termination. (c) Remedies may include reinstatement, back pay, and damages.

(a) Every resident individual shall pay an annual tax on his entire net income from all sources. (b) The tax shall be computed at the following rates: (1) 1 percent on the first $1,000.00 of taxable income; (2) 2 percent on the next $2,000.00 of taxable income; (3) 3 percent on the next $2,000.00 of taxable income; (4) 4 percent on the next $2,000.00 of taxable income; (5) 5 percent on the next $2,000.00 of taxable income; and (6) 5.75 percent on all taxable income in excess of $10,000.00. (c) The tax shall be due and payable on or before April 15 following the close of the taxable year.

(a) Any person of sound mind and 14 years of age or older may make a will. (b) A will must be in writing, signed by the testator, and attested by at least two witnesses. (c) A will may be handwritten (holographic) if entirely in the testator's handwriting and signed by the testator. (d) A will may be revoked by a subsequent will, codicil, or physical act.

(a) If a person dies without a valid will, his property passes by intestate succession. (b) The intestate share of a surviving spouse is: (1) The entire estate if there are no surviving descendants; (2) Three-fourths of the estate if there are surviving descendants, all of whom are also descendants of the surviving spouse; or (3) One-half of the estate if there are surviving descendants who are not descendants of the surviving spouse. (c) If there is no surviving spouse, the estate passes to the descendants per stirpes. (d) If there are no descendants, the estate passes to the parents or their descendants.

(a) A person commits the offense of rape when he has carnal knowledge of a female forcibly and against her will. Carnal knowledge in rape occurs when there is any penetration of the female sex organ by the male sex organ. (b) A person convicted of the offense of rape shall be punished by imprisonment for not less than 25 years nor more than life. (c) A person convicted of the offense of rape shall not be eligible for parole until the minimum term has been served.

(a) A person commits the offense of aggravated sodomy when he or she commits sodomy with force and against the will of the other person. (b) A person convicted of the offense of aggravated sodomy shall be punished by imprisonment for not less than 25 years nor more than life. (c) A person convicted of the offense of aggravated sodomy shall not be eligible for parole until the minimum term has been served.

(a) A person commits the offense of burglary when, without authority and with the intent to commit a felony or theft therein, he or she enters or remains within the dwelling house of another or any building, vehicle, railroad car, or other structure designed for use as the dwelling of another or enters or remains within any other building, railroad car, or structure with the intent to commit a felony or theft therein. (b) A person convicted of the offense of burglary shall be punished by imprisonment for not less than five nor more than 20 years.

(a) A person commits the offense of theft by deception when he or she obtains property by any deceitful means or artful practice with the intention of depriving the owner of the property. (b) A person convicted of the offense of theft by deception shall be punished by imprisonment for not less than one nor more than ten years.

(a) A person commits the offense of forgery in the first degree when, with intent to defraud, he or she knowingly makes, alters, or possesses any writing in a fictitious name or in such manner that the writing as made or altered purports to have been made by another person, at another time, with different provisions, or by authority of one who did not give such authority. (b) A person convicted of forgery in the first degree shall be punished by imprisonment for not less than one nor more than 15 years.

(a) A person commits the offense of arson in the first degree when he or she maliciously damages any building or vehicle by fire or explosive. (b) A person convicted of arson in the first degree shall be punished by imprisonment for not less than ten nor more than 20 years.

(a) A contract is an agreement between two or more parties for the doing or not doing of some specified thing. (b) To constitute a valid contract, there must be parties able to contract, a consideration moving to the contract, the assent of the parties to the terms of the contract, and a subject matter upon which the contract can operate. (c) The term 'contract' includes all agreements, whether written or oral, express or implied.

(a) To constitute consideration, a performance or a return promise must be bargained for. (b) A performance or return promise is bargained for if it is sought by the promisor in exchange for his promise and is given by the promisee in exchange for that promise. (c) The performance may consist of an act other than a promise, or a forbearance, or the creation, modification, or destruction of a legal relation.

(a) All persons are capable of contracting except minors, persons of unsound mind, and persons deprived of civil rights. (b) A minor may disaffirm a contract at any time during minority or within a reasonable time after reaching majority. (c) A contract made by a person of unsound mind may be avoided if the other party knew or should have known of the mental incapacity.

(a) A contract for the sale of goods for the price of $500.00 or more is not enforceable by way of action or defense unless there is some writing sufficient to indicate that a contract for sale has been made between the parties and signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought. (b) A contract for the sale of real property is not enforceable unless the promise or agreement, or some note or memorandum thereof, is in writing and signed by the party to be charged.

(a) A breach of contract occurs when a party fails to perform his or her obligations under the contract. (b) The non-breaching party may recover damages for any loss resulting from the breach. (c) Damages may include compensatory damages, consequential damages, and in some cases, punitive damages. (d) Specific performance may be ordered when money damages are inadequate.

(a) A person shall not drive or be in actual physical control of any moving vehicle while: (1) Under the influence of alcohol to the extent that it is less safe for the person to drive; (2) Under the influence of any drug to the extent that it is less safe for the person to drive; or (3) Under the combined influence of alcohol and a drug to the extent that it is less safe for the person to drive. (b) A person convicted of violating subsection (a) of this Code section shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.

(a) Any person who drives any vehicle with willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property is guilty of reckless driving. Violation of the provisions of this Code section is a misdemeanor punishable by imprisonment for not less than ten days nor more than 12 months. (b) Upon a second conviction within a five-year period of time, the defendant shall be guilty of a high and aggravated misdemeanor.

(a) No person shall drive a vehicle on any highway of this state at a speed greater than is reasonable and prudent under the conditions and having regard for the actual and potential hazards then existing. (b) In every event, speed shall be so controlled as may be necessary to avoid colliding with any person, vehicle, or other conveyance on or entering the highway in compliance with legal requirements and the duty of all persons to use due care. (c) Except when a special hazard exists that requires lower speed for compliance with paragraph (2) of subsection (b) of this Code section, the limits specified in this Code section or established as authorized in this chapter shall be maximum lawful speeds, and no person shall drive a vehicle on any highway at a speed in excess of such maximum limits.
